role: Attempts real forgery attacks against the audit Merkle chain mechanism D-03 verifies, surfacing the genuine limitation that pure hash-chain self-consistency is not tamper-evident without an externally-anchored chain tip.
behaviorDescription: attemptNaiveTamper() changes one event's content without recomputing anything downstream — verifyChain() correctly catches this. attemptConsistentReforge() changes one event's content AND correctly re-links every subsequent event using the real linkEvent() function, the same function an honest chain-builder uses — verifyChain() reports this as fully valid, which is the genuine finding this bot exists to surface, not a bug in D-03. Every attempt operates on a deep clone of the input chain (the caller's original is never mutated) and is recorded/signaled through the isolated red-team bus and decision store, never the production ones.
hardStops: Never operates on a live chain reference — every attempt runs against a deep clone via cloneTarget()
Never signals or persists through the production swarmSignalBus or bot_decisions table — isolated via RedTeamBot
Never claims to attack SLH-DSA specifically — @platform/pqcrypto doesn't exist; this attacks the real SHA-256 chain mechanism that does exist
